p: And the version of the Geonim reads:

that "le'itah" is feeding done by another,
"That wicked one opened his mouth wide like a camel.
He said to him: I will open my mouth,
and you keep on pouring in —
as we learned," and so on,
"but one may feed by pouring into the mouth."
And this is like what was prayed for by
Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him:
וְנָתַן לִי לֶחֶם לֶאֱכוֹל [שָׁם כח, כ],
"And He will give me bread to eat" (ibid. 28:20).
Seemingly the word "to eat" is superfluous,
for it is obvious that bread is for eating.
And we said that the intent is
שֶׁה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ יִהְיֶה הַמַּאֲכִיל גַּם כֵּן.
that Hashem Yisbarach should also be the One who feeds.
וְהָיָה צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר תֵּן לִי טֶרֶף.
